meta.subtitle: Deep-value pet e-commerce leader compounding margin and free cash flow, controlled by BC Partners

analystCommentary: We rate Chewy a BUY with a target range of $20 to $31 against a current price of $18.61, which sits near the bottom of its $17.40 to $40.55 52-week range. Our probability-weighted fair value is about $24, an expected upside near 32%, with a bear-case downside around 25% and a reward/risk of roughly 1.28x. The case is a profitable, cash-generative category leader that the market has de-rated hard: net sales grew 7.3% to $3.33 billion in the fiscal second quarter ended August 2, 2026, Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 90 basis points to 6.8%, and Autoship reached 84.6% of net sales. Consensus is constructive with a $28.82 target, about 55% above the current price. We hold to a BUY rather than a stronger call for two reasons: the low forward multiple rests on adjusted earnings that exclude large share-based compensation, and BC Partners controls 88.4% of the voting power, which limits minority shareholder influence.

executiveSummary.companyOverview: Chewy is a leading online pet retailer in the United States, founded in 2010 and based in Plantation, Florida. It sells pet food and treats, supplies, medications and pet-health products, plus services such as telehealth, pet insurance offerings and veterinary clinics, through its websites and mobile apps. The company partners with approximately 4,000 brands and offers approximately 190,000 products, and its Autoship subscription program is the core driver of recurring revenue. FY26, the fiscal year ended February 1, 2026, produced net sales of $12.6 billion, up 6.2%, at a gross margin of 29.8%. Chewy reports as a single segment and has a dual-class share structure under which BC Partners, through Argos Holdings, holds all of the Class B stock.

thesis.body: The thesis is a de-rated leader whose profitability is improving faster than its top line. Net sales rose 7.3% to $3.33 billion in the fiscal second quarter, but Adjusted EBITDA grew far faster as margin expanded, and Autoship's dominant share of sales gives the revenue base durability. At 12.1x next-twelve-months and roughly 10x FY28E adjusted earnings, with the stock near its 52-week low, the valuation prices in little of that margin trajectory. The offsets are real: the low multiple is measured on adjusted earnings that add back heavy share-based compensation, unit growth has slowed, and BC Partners' voting control removes the usual shareholder checks. Our BUY reflects a reward/risk skewed to the upside while those offsets keep us from a stronger call.

catalysts: Margin expansion: Adjusted EBITDA rose 23.7% year over year in the fiscal second quarter as the Adjusted EBITDA margin reached 6.8%, and management raised its full-year revenue and profitability outlook.
Recurring revenue: Autoship customer sales grew 9.3% to $2,817.2 million, outpacing total net-sales growth and lifting Autoship's already-dominant share of the mix.
Cash generation and buybacks: FY26 free cash flow was $562.4 million, funding $262.5 million of share repurchases with no dividend.
Recent acquisitions: the SmartPak and Modern Animal deals broaden the platform and contributed customers in the quarter.
A consensus target of $28.82, about 55% above the current price, with 18 of 26 analysts rating the shares Buy.
risks: Slowing growth: organic sales and active-customer gains have decelerated.
Adjusted-earnings quality: the low forward multiple relies on adjusted figures that add back heavy share-based compensation.
Controlled company: BC Partners' voting control leaves minority holders little influence over the board or strategy.
Consumer discretionary exposure: a weaker economy or reduced pet spending would pressure a low-margin, high-volume model.
Strong internet-based competition in pet retail limits pricing power.

financials.incomeCommentary: Net sales in the fiscal second quarter ended August 2, 2026 were $3,330.2 million, up 7.3% year over year, or 5.7% excluding the SmartPak and Modern Animal acquisitions. (The vendor snapshot labels this period Q3 on a calendar basis; it is the company's fiscal second quarter, since Chewy's 52/53-week year ends near the end of January.) Gross margin was 30.4% in the quarter. Income from operations was $92.0 million, a 2.8% operating margin, and net income rose 29.8% to $80.5 million, with diluted EPS of $0.20. Adjusted EBITDA rose to $226.7 million, a 6.8% margin, and adjusted diluted EPS was $0.36. For FY26 the company reported net income of $222.8 million and diluted EPS of $0.52; the year-over-year decline from the prior $0.91 is an artifact of a $275.7 million deferred-tax valuation-allowance release that had boosted the prior year, not a deterioration in operations. On an adjusted basis FY26 diluted EPS was $1.27, up $0.23, and consensus estimates call for $1.54 in FY27E and $1.87 in FY28E. Reported GAAP net income includes FY26 share-based compensation and related taxes of $311.2 million.
financials.balanceCommentary: The balance sheet took on debt to fund acquisitions. As of August 2, 2026 the company held $611.0 million of cash and $1.2 million of marketable securities, against long-term debt of $588.7 million plus a $3.0 million current portion, drawn during the year to fund SmartPak and Modern Animal. Goodwill rose to $334.1 million from $39.4 million and intangible assets to $149.7 million, reflecting those deals. Total stockholders' equity was $370.5 million, still against an accumulated deficit of $1,184.8 million from the company's earlier loss-making years. Interest coverage was a comfortable 28.8x on a trailing basis, so the new debt is modest relative to earnings, and the current ratio of 0.84 is normal for a fast-turning retailer that funds inventory partly through payables.
financials.cashflowCommentary: Cash generation is the strongest part of the story. FY26 operating cash flow was $691.6 million and capital expenditure was $129.2 million, producing free cash flow of $562.4 million, up $109.9 million year over year at a rising free-cash-flow margin. The company pays no dividend and returns cash through buybacks, repurchasing $262.5 million of stock in FY26 after a larger program the prior year. Free cash flow comfortably covers the buyback and the light capital budget, though a portion of reported profitability is non-cash share-based compensation, so cash returns are a cleaner gauge of value creation here than GAAP earnings.

valuation.multiplesCommentary: The shares trade at 28.2x trailing GAAP earnings and 0.6x sales, falling to 12.1x next-twelve-months and about 10x FY28E on adjusted consensus earnings. The gap between the trailing GAAP multiple and the forward multiple is wide because the forward estimates are adjusted, most importantly for share-based compensation, which is a recurring cost. No relevant peer multiple set was available in this pack, so we value the company on its own forward earnings, its free-cash-flow generation and the durability of Autoship revenue. The scenarios turn on whether margin expansion continues and whether growth stabilizes.

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Margin expansion continues toward the high-single-digit Adjusted EBITDA range, active-customer and Autoship growth stabilize, and sentiment recovers, re-rating the shares toward the analyst consensus. Implied price near $33, above the median $29.00 target and toward the $36.00 top of the analyst range.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: Net sales compound in the mid-single digits, Adjusted EBITDA margin keeps expanding modestly, and the market pays a mid-teens multiple on adjusted earnings that still discounts the share-based-compensation add-back. Implied price about $24, below the $28.82 consensus target.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Pet spending softens, unit growth stalls, and margin gains slow, so the market keeps the multiple depressed and the shares fall below their 52-week low. Implied price near $14, roughly 25% below the current $18.61 and under the $17.40 low of the range.

valuation.scenarioCommentary: Weighting the Bull at 30%, the Base at 48% and the Bear at 22% gives a fair value of about $24, an expected upside near 32% and a bear-case downside of roughly 25%, for a reward/risk of about 1.28x. The risk/reward on the numbers would support a stronger rating; we hold to BUY because the Bear is a genuine scenario for a discretionary retailer whose growth has slowed, and because the adjusted-earnings basis and BC Partners' voting control both argue for a discount to the headline consensus. The Base intentionally applies a lower multiple than the Street to reflect the share-based-compensation adjustment.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Chewy reports as a single segment: an integrated e-commerce platform for pet products, health and services. Revenue spans consumables (retail pet food and veterinary diets), hard goods (non-perishable supplies), pet health and specialty products including prescription medications, and other sales such as private brands and services. The defining characteristic is recurring demand: Autoship customer sales reached $2,817.2 million in the fiscal second quarter, 84.6% of net sales, providing automatic reorder and payment that lifts retention. Active customers numbered 21.7 million with net sales per active customer of $602, and the platform carries roughly 190,000 products from about 4,000 brands.

moatFactors.name: Autoship recurring revenue
moatFactors.body: The Autoship subscription program drove the large majority of net sales in the fiscal second quarter and grew 9.3% year over year, creating predictable reorders and high retention that a general retailer cannot easily replicate for the pet category.

moatFactors.name: Selection and category focus
moatFactors.body: The breadth of the catalog across pet categories, plus private brands and pet-health offerings including prescription pharmacy, makes Chewy a one-stop destination whose depth in a single category is hard to match at scale.

moatFactors.name: Fulfillment and service scale
moatFactors.body: A national fulfillment network and a service-led model, extended by its pharmacy, telehealth, veterinary-clinic and insurance offerings and by the SmartPak and Modern Animal acquisitions, raise the practical cost for customers to switch away from the platform.

moatFactors.name: Low switching costs and big-retailer competition
moatFactors.body: The 10-K flags strong internet-based competition in the pet products and services industry, which can undercut price, caps pricing power and keeps the moat narrow.

businessMoat.durability: The moat is narrow but improving. Autoship's recurring, high-retention revenue and the category depth are durable advantages, and the move into pharmacy, insurance and veterinary services deepens engagement. The offset is that pet e-commerce has low switching costs and faces strong internet-based competition, so durability depends on continuing to convert customers to Autoship and on the service ecosystem raising retention faster than competition erodes it.

points: Autoship's rising share of sales shifts the mix toward recurring, higher-retention revenue.
Operating leverage: operating expenses grew more slowly than net sales in the quarter, widening the operating margin.
The SmartPak and Modern Animal acquisitions extend the platform into adjacent pet categories and services.
Consensus revenue growth to roughly $13.5 billion in FY27E and $14.4 billion in FY28E extends the mid-single-digit top-line trajectory.
Expansion of pet-health and pharmacy offerings can lift spending per active customer over time.

management.leadership: Sumit Singh is Chief Executive Officer, and Raymond Svider serves as Chairperson, so the chair and chief-executive roles are separated. The company saw finance and technology leadership turnover in the period: David Reeder resigned as Chief Financial Officer effective July 3, 2025; Chris Deppe was appointed Chief Financial Officer effective February 2026; and Satish Mehta resigned as Chief Technology Officer effective February 2026. William Billings serves as Chief Accounting Officer and was interim principal financial officer between those appointments.
management.capitalAllocation: The company pays no dividend and allocates cash to buybacks and acquisitions. It repurchased $262.5 million of stock in FY26, following a larger program the prior year, and used newly drawn debt to fund the SmartPak and Modern Animal acquisitions. Executive pay is heavily weighted to equity with performance and service vesting conditions, which aligns management with the share price but also drives the large share-based-compensation charge that separates adjusted from GAAP earnings.
management.governance: Chewy is a 'controlled company' under NYSE rules because BC Partners, through Argos Holdings, holds all of the Class B common stock and 88.4% of the total voting power. As a result the company is exempt from certain independence requirements, including that a majority of the board and the full compensation and nominating committees be independent. The board has determined six directors independent: Kristine Dickson, Deborah Ellinger, Nat Goldhaber, James Nelson, Martin Nesbitt and James Star. Minority shareholders therefore have limited ability to influence board composition or strategy, which is the central governance consideration in the stock.
management.insiderOwnership: Voting control rests with BC Partners, which beneficially owns all 176,478,229 Class B shares, 100% of that class and the controlling share of total voting power, as of the May 13, 2026 record date. Individual insider economic stakes are small: CEO Sumit Singh held 1,020,477 Class A shares and all current directors and executive officers as a group held 1,404,507, each less than 1%. Among institutions holding Class A, BlackRock owned 8.3%, AQR 7.0% and Vanguard 5.2%, but none of that translates into control given the Class B voting power.

idiosyncratic: Growth maturity: net sales grew 5.7% excluding acquisitions and active customers rose 3.8% to 21.7 million, so the top line depends increasingly on spending more per customer and on acquired businesses.
Earnings quality: the forward multiple relies on adjusted earnings that exclude share-based compensation, which was $85.9 million in the fiscal second quarter and remains a recurring, dilutive cost.
Governance: BC Partners' 88.4% voting control means minority holders cannot influence the board, and the controlled-company exemptions reduce independent oversight of compensation and nominations.
Management transition: turnover in the CFO and CTO roles during the period adds execution risk as new leaders settle in.
Integration risk: the SmartPak and Modern Animal acquisitions must be integrated and earn their goodwill, and acquired growth can mask softer organic trends.
risks.systemic: Chewy's demand is tied to consumer discretionary spending on pets, which the company's quarterly MD&A notes is sensitive to inflationary pressures, elevated interest rates and broader economic uncertainty. A downturn that reduces pet adoption or spending would pressure a low-margin, high-volume model, and the company competes in a strong, internet-based competitive environment. Shipping and fulfillment costs, subject to fuel and labor inflation, are a further systemic exposure for an e-commerce business that ships virtually all of its sales. These forces would weigh on both volumes and the multiple investors assign to future margin gains.

body: We rate Chewy a BUY with a $20 to $31 target range around a probability-weighted fair value of about $24. The company is a de-rated category leader improving where it matters: fiscal second-quarter net sales rose 7.3% to $3.33 billion, Adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 6.8%, Autoship reached its high share of sales, and FY26 free cash flow was $562.4 million, funding buybacks with no dividend.

We stop at a moderate BUY rather than a stronger call because two things temper the deep-value read. The forward multiple near 10 to 12 times is measured on adjusted earnings that add back heavy share-based compensation, so the stock is less cheap on a GAAP basis, and BC Partners' 88.4% voting control leaves minority holders with little say. The Bear, about 25% below the current price, is the case where pet spending softens and the multiple stays depressed. With the shares near their 52-week low and cash generation strong, we would accumulate in the lower half of our range and size for the governance and growth risks.
